Hi Anna,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Per our call, a few quick clarifying points on Redwood's default behavior and options around data retention, deletion SLAs, and backups so you can share with the security & legal teams: 

- Data persistence: inference request payloads and generated outputs are ephemeral in the hosted API by default; we keep request/response logs for debugging and billing for 90 days unless a customer requests a longer retention or has Dedicated/Private deployment requirements.
- Deletion SLA: for hosted accounts, a complete deletion request (application data + request logs + cached KV) is handled within 30 days. We can provide an expedited 7-day process under an enterprise contract.
- Backups & snapshots: system backups (for Dedicated and Private) are rolling snapshots encrypted at rest; default snapshot retention is 90 days. For Private deployments, we support configurable retention (30/90/365 days) per contract.
- Audit logs: audit and admin action logs retained 365 days for Dedicated customers; hosted accounts have 90-day retention for admin/audit trails.
- Encryption & keys: data is encrypted in transit and at rest; customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are available on Private and Dedicated.

Hi Anna — quick technical clarifications on backups and deletion process: 

- Backup architecture: hosted accounts: we maintain encrypted incremental backups stored in object storage with lifecycle policies; snapshots are created nightly. For Dedicated, customers may opt into cross-region replication.
- Deletion from backups: because backups are stored as immutable incremental chain objects, a full rebuild without the deleted objects requires an overwrite workflow and lifecycle expiration. This means a mechanically immediate purge from backups is non-trivial for hosted systems; we therefore surface an expedited purge process that marks objects for deletion and accelerates lifecycle expiration (contractually agreed). Typical expedited purge timelines: 7–30 days depending on the retention tier and snapshot compaction schedule.
- Logs with PHI: we do not recommend sending PHI to hosted log aggregators; for HIPAA workloads customers should use Dedicated/Private + BAA and customer-managed logging endpoints.
- Verification: we can provide attestation evidence when a deletion request is completed (deletion ticket id + audit log snippet).
